title: Major iron ore producers have used 11.1 billion tonnes of reserves over the past decade replacing three-fourths of tonnes mined
gist: The six largest iron ore producers depleted 11.1 billion tonnes of marketable reserves between FY2016 and FY2025 and only three fully replaced what they mined, with net replacement ratios spanning 28% to 159%. Rising strip ratios have roughly doubled C1 cash costs for some producers, cash margins have converged to US$50-60 per tonne, reserve grades have slipped by up to 1.6 percentage points with rising alumina, and growth capex per tonne of reserve added varies fivefold from about US$2 to US$10, leaving the industry investing heavily just to hold output flat.

insights.claim: Between FY2016 and FY2025 the six largest iron ore producers collectively depleted 11.1 billion tonnes of marketable reserves, and only three of them replaced what they mined over the period.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Half the majors are shrinking their resource base; long-dated iron ore supply curves built on flat output from incumbents are optimistic.
insights.quote: Between FY2016 and FY2025, the six largest iron ore producers collectively depleted 11.1 billion tonnes of marketable reserves. However, only three of them replaced what they mined over the period

insights.claim: Net reserve replacement ratios across the iron ore peer group ranged from 28% to 159%, reflecting differences in reserve conversion, capital allocation and operational disruptions.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A near sixfold dispersion in replacement performance is a screening metric for which producers own the next decade of volume and which face a cliff.
insights.quote: Net reserve replacement ratios across the peer group ranged from 28% to 159%, reflecting differences in reserve conversion, capital allocation and operational disruptions.

insights.claim: Producers carrying 15 or more years of reserve life retain a meaningful buffer, so depletion is not yet an acute crisis for the whole peer group.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Tempers the alarmism: the trade is relative, across producers with differing reserve lives, not a sector-wide supply shock.
insights.quote: Many producers still have long reserve lives, with those carrying 15 or more years retaining a meaningful buffer

insights.claim: As mine lives shorten the margin for error narrows and each successive tonne becomes more challenging and costly to replace, making the direction of travel unambiguous even where buffers remain.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Implies a structurally rising incentive price for iron ore over the next decade regardless of near-term demand.
insights.quote: But the direction of travel is clear: as mine lives shorten, the margin for error narrows, and each successive tonne becomes more challenging and costly to replace.

insights.claim: C1 cash costs have risen sharply across the iron ore industry since FY2016, roughly doubling for some producers over the period.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Cost-curve inflation of this scale lifts the price floor beneath iron ore and compresses the low-cost moat the majors historically enjoyed.
insights.quote: C1 cash costs have risen sharply across the industry since FY2016, roughly doubling for some producers over the period.

insights.claim: As ore bodies mature, more waste material must be moved to access the same volume of ore, a rising strip ratio effect that reflects natural mine maturity and is expected to persist.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Cost inflation here is geological, not cyclical, so it will not reverse when diesel, labour or freight costs normalise.
insights.quote: As ore bodies mature, more waste material must be moved to access the same volume of ore. This reflects the natural progression of mine maturity and is expected to persist.

insights.claim: Cash margins peaked across the iron ore industry in FY2021 and by FY2025 had converged to approximately US$50-60 per tonne across the peer group after cost inflation.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Margin convergence around US$50-60/t is the number to stress-test against any iron ore price scenario below current levels.
insights.quote: By FY2025, margins across the peer group had converged to approximately US$50–60 per tonne

insights.claim: The narrowing margin buffer reduces the iron ore industry's capacity to absorb further input cost increases or sustained periods of price weakness without affecting investment decisions.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A sustained price drawdown now triggers capex deferral faster than in past cycles, which is ultimately supply-supportive for prices.
insights.quote: The narrowing of this buffer reduces the industry's capacity to absorb further input cost increases or sustained periods of price weakness without affecting investment decisions.

insights.claim: The overall quality of iron reserves has stayed mostly steady, but the mix producing that stability is changing, with reserve grade falling by as much as 1.6 percentage points among some peers since 2016.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Headline stability masks individual deterioration; grade decline is a producer-specific differentiator hidden by peer-group averages.
insights.quote: The overall quality of iron reserves has stayed mostly steady, but the mix that makes up this stability is changing.

insights.claim: Higher-grade material is increasingly required to offset the depletion of lower-grade ore bodies, while impurity levels, particularly alumina, are rising in some product streams.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Producers are burning through their best blending stock to hold product specs, a hidden depletion of quality optionality.
insights.quote: Higher-grade material is increasingly required to offset the depletion of lower-grade ore bodies, while impurity levels, particularly alumina, are rising in some product streams.

insights.claim: Alumina attracts specific penalties in blast furnace operations independent of overall iron content, so producers whose product quality drifts toward higher impurity face a structural pricing headwind compounding rising production costs.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Realised price, not just benchmark price, is where the damage shows up; model impurity penalties separately from Fe grade.
insights.quote: Alumina attracts specific penalties in blast furnace operations, independent of overall iron content.

insights.claim: Some iron ore producers have moved from a modest realised premium to a persistent discount to the 62% Fe benchmark over the past five years, driven by falling product iron content combined with rising impurity levels.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Benchmark-linked revenue models overstate these producers' earnings; track realised-price-to-benchmark spreads as a deteriorating fundamental.
insights.quote: some producers have moved from a modest, realised premium to a persistent discount to the 62% Fe benchmark over the past five years

insights.claim: The premium segment of the iron ore market remains concentrated among a small number of producers, and new entrants face a high bar because achieving consistent benchmark quality requires operational maturity that takes time to establish.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Incumbent premium producers keep a durable moat; new greenfield supply is unlikely to compete on quality quickly, supporting high-grade premiums.
insights.quote: New entrants seeking to compete in this segment face a high bar, with achieving consistent benchmark quality requiring operational maturity that takes time to establish.

insights.claim: Reserve replacement ratios tell only part of the story because the quality of replacement resources is not always equivalent to what was mined, with some operations experiencing grade erosion and rising impurity levels over time.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Use a quality-adjusted replacement metric, not headline tonnes replaced, when comparing miners' resource sustainability.
insights.quote: Reserve replacement ratios tell only part of the story. While several producers have successfully replenished depleted tonnes, the quality of those replacement resources is not always equivalent

insights.claim: Cumulative growth capital expenditure per tonne of iron ore reserve added between 2016 and 2025 ranged from approximately US$2 per tonne up to US$10 per tonne across the major producers.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A fivefold spread in the cost of buying back a tonne of reserve is a direct, comparable measure of capital efficiency across miners.
insights.quote: cumulative growth capital expenditure per tonne of reserve added between 2016 and 2025 found outcomes ranging from approximately US$2 per tonne up to US$10 per tonne

insights.claim: The fivefold difference in replacement capital intensity reflects the varying quality of remaining resource pipelines as well as operational and regulatory challenges experienced across the peer group.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Permitting and resource-pipeline quality, not management skill alone, drive the capital-efficiency gap; weigh jurisdiction in valuations.
insights.quote: This fivefold difference reflects the varying quality of remaining resource pipelines, as well as the operational and regulatory challenges experienced across the peer group.

insights.claim: As existing ore bodies mature, producers face a growing need to invest not simply to expand supply but to replace what they have already mined.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Reframes miner capex: a rising share is maintenance-equivalent, so headline growth capex overstates future volume growth and free cash flow durability.
insights.quote: producers face a growing need to invest not simply to expand supply, but to replace what they have already mined

themes.theme: Sustaining capex, not a supply step-change

insights.claim: Several major iron ore producers have committed billions of dollars to brownfield expansions and sustaining projects over the coming decade, designed to replace depleting ore bodies and maintain production on a broadly like-for-like volume basis.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Large announced project pipelines should not be read as future supply growth; they are volume defence.
insights.quote: These projects are designed to replace depleting ore bodies and maintain production on a broadly like-for-like volume basis.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie characterises the major producers' investment as largely sustaining in nature, designed to maintain existing production levels rather than deliver a step-change in available supply.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Removes a commonly assumed source of future seaborne supply growth, a medium-term support for iron ore prices if demand holds.
insights.quote: Wood Mackenzie's analysis characterises this investment as largely sustaining in nature.

insights.claim: The iron ore industry is entering a period in which the effort, capital and technical complexity required to hold output flat is materially greater than it was a decade ago.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The central investable conclusion: flat volumes now cost more, so margin and free cash flow per tonne compress even in stable price environments.
insights.quote: The iron ore industry is therefore entering a period in which the effort, capital and technical complexity required to hold output flat is materially greater than it was a decade ago.

insights.claim: The main challenge for the current iron ore industry is rising costs to maintain existing production, with the sector investing to sustain output but having to work harder to stand still.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Frames iron ore as a cost-inflation story rather than a depletion story; watch unit costs and realised premiums over reserve headlines.
insights.quote: The industry is investing to sustain production, but it is having to work harder to stand still.
